title: Taking Down the Wing Gambit!! | Deep Dive | Sicilian | GM Naroditsky's Theory Speed Run

moves.spoken: The Sicilian, aiming for the Accelerated Dragon.

White offers the Wing Gambit with b4 — a third-string gambit with a dubious reputation. Its idea is the usual one: deflect our c-pawn off c5 so White can occupy the center with d4. But here Black is objectively better with accurate play.
teaches: the Wing Gambit idea and its flaw

moves.spoken: We accept with the c-pawn, not the knight — taking with the knight would hand White a tempo to play c3 and prop up his center.
teaches: accept with the pawn to deny White c3 with tempo

moves.spoken: White plays d4 as expected, and the move on everyone's mind should be d5 — contesting the center before it's too late, and the queen can't even be hit by a knight to c3 because our pawn covers that square.

Here, though, a practical choice — the modest d6. It's probably a shade worse than d5, but it drags a theory-armed opponent onto their own thinking, and it does a fine job stopping White's e-pawn while we've lost almost no development.
teaches: a modest off-theory move to make the opponent think

moves.spoken: The knight swings to e5 to fight for a central pawn of our own; and note the trade is safe — a check on b5 just runs into the bishop to d7, so our queen is never in danger.
teaches: Ne5 for a center pawn, with ...Bd7 covering the check
